extracted.subtask_description: A newsroom style guide for writing about race, ethnicity, religion, disability, gender and related social topics; provides preferred terms, avoidances, capitalization and explanatory background for many entries used in news reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: reservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Indian reservations are areas of land reserved by the U.S. government as permanent tribal homelands. The United States established its reservation policy for American Indians in 1787. In 2015 there were 326 reservations. About 56 million acres are in reservations and trust land. More than 60 percent of American Indians live away from reservations.

rubrics_metrics.name: residential care homes
rubrics_metrics.description: Residential care homes offer personalized services to small groups of adults who live together in a home. These homes provide lodging, meal services and assistance with daily living activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other terms include adult family homes, board and care homes, or personal care homes.

rubrics_metrics.name: retarded
rubrics_metrics.description: See mentally retarded, mentally disabled, intellectually disabled, developmentally disabled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The entry indicates cross-reference to preferred, people-first and less offensive alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: reverse discrimination, reverse racism
rubrics_metrics.description: These phrases are used in lawsuits and in accusations that affirmative action puts men and non-minorities at a disadvantage for college admission, scholarships and jobs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research shows that this scarcely happens. A 1995 Brandeis University study of 3,000 discrimination suits found that about 100 had charged reverse discrimination; the court ordered relief in six of those cases. Use the phrase with caution and context; do not present it as a common or likely outcome without evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roma, Romany, Romani
rubrics_metrics.description: The Roma, or Romani (also spelled Romany) are a traditionally itinerant ethnic group, who live mostly in Europe; branches of the ethnic group live in the Americas, Asia and North Africa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They are often called Gypsies (or Gipsies) but that term has negative connotations of illegal activity and many Roma don't identify with it. Romany usually refers specifically to Romanichals in England. Note linguistic and genetic evidence suggesting origins in northern India. Distinguish Roma from Irish Travelers; mention historic persecution and continuing discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roman Catholic Church
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the largest Christian community in the world and in the U.S. The Roman Catholic Church considers itself to be the one, true, and full expression of the church founded by Jesus Christ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains origins tied to Church of Rome, Petrine/papal authority, seven sacraments, hierarchical structure (pope, cardinal, archbishop, bishop, monsignor, priest, deacon), organization (Holy See, Vatican, archdioceses, dioceses). Notes women are barred from holy orders. Use 'Roman Catholic Church' terminology and capitalization guidance as given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rosh Hashanah
rubrics_metrics.description: Pronounced 'rohsh-huh-SHAH-nuh.' The Jewish New Year, celebrated according to the Hebrew calendar sometime between the middle of September and the middle of October.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To find exact dates consult Jewish holidays resources such as Hebcal.

rubrics_metrics.name: rumspringa
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Amish allow their youth, after age 16, to spend a couple years free of the most intense restrictions of their faith while still living with their parents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to ensure commitment to faith before baptism; the vast majority decide to remain within the Amish community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Russian Orthodox Church
rubrics_metrics.description: Branch of the Eastern Church of Christianity with headquarters in Moscow. It is the largest of the national and ethnic churches of Eastern Orthodoxy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Eastern Orthodox for broader context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sabbath
rubrics_metrics.description: The day of the week observed for rest and worship. Most Christian traditions observe the Sabbath on Sunday; Judaism and some Christian traditions observe it on Saturday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize 'Sabbath' in religious references but lowercase when talking about periods of rest.

rubrics_metrics.name: safe neighborhood, bad neighborhood
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid judgmental terms about neighborhoods or districts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use more specific terms such as low-income neighborhood or areas with high crime rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: safe sex, safer sex
rubrics_metrics.description: Sexual practices that minimize the possible transmission of HIV and other infectious agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some publications prefer 'safer sex' to denote that no sexual contact is completely safe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sambo
rubrics_metrics.description: Historically, term was used to describe a happy black slave. Today, it is an offensive term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use in copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: sandsucker
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Racial slur; derogatory term for Arabs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sansei, sansei
rubrics_metrics.description: Term for third-generation Japanese Americans, originating from the Japanese language term for 'third generation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains generational terms Issei (first generation), Nisei (second), Sansei (third), Yonsei (fourth). Notes capitalization practices vary by institution and context; capitalize in generational context or proper nouns, otherwise lowercase when referring to an individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanskrit
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanskrit is one of the oldest languages in the world that is still being used and is the root for many other languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often used for religion and ceremony; note script usage (Devanagari) varies. Refer to Omniglot for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: sari (also saree)
rubrics_metrics.description: A traditional garment worn by a women in India, Bangladesh, Nepal and Sri Lanka, essentially a piece of fabric about 6 yards long that is wrapped around the body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe general wearing style (wrapped around waist, draped over shoulder) and note variations in fabric, style and price; sometimes worn with a blouse.

rubrics_metrics.name: schizo, schizoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slang words derived from schizophrenic and generally used inaccurately. Use precise alternatives: indecisive or unsettled, as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: schizophrenia, schizophrenic
rubrics_metrics.description: A severe and chronic mental illness characterized by distorted recognition and interpretations of reality, affecting how an individual thinks, feels and acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common symptoms described; avoid using 'schizophrenic' as an adjective. Use people-first language (person with schizophrenia) and refer only if formally diagnosed and relevant. Do not use for nonpsychiatric conditions. Similar guidance applies to terms like psychotic, bipolar, anorexic and OCD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scotch, Scots, Scottish
rubrics_metrics.description: All three words may be defined as 'of or relating to Scotland' but in modern usage they have different connotations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Scottish' as the preferred adjective for people, culture or ancestry. 'Scots' often refers to the dialect. 'Scotch' is generally used for certain food products or Scotch whisky.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scottsboro
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical summary of the 1931 Scottsboro case in Alabama in which nine black teenagers were falsely accused of rape; became a symbol of racism and injustice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives historical context including retrials, protests, Supreme Court rulings, and eventual pardons.

rubrics_metrics.name: sect
rubrics_metrics.description: Refers to a group that has broken off from another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid this label unless you are sure it fits; it often carries negative connotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 8, Housing Choice Voucher Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 8 is a common shorthand for the Housing Choice Voucher Program, funded by HUD to help very low-income families, older people and disabled people afford housing in the private market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Housing Choice Voucher Program is the more accurate and current term; 'Section 8' refers to Section 8 of the United States Housing Act of 1937.

rubrics_metrics.name: secular humanism
rubrics_metrics.description: An outlook that emphasizes human rather than religious values, stressing reason, scientific inquiry, individual freedom and responsibility, human values and compassion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes the emphasis on tolerance and cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: secularism
rubrics_metrics.description: The belief that religion and religious considerations have no place in public life and education.

rubrics_metrics.name: seder
rubrics_metrics.description: The ritualized dinner held in Jewish homes on the first night or first two nights of Passover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Means 'order' in Hebrew; commemorates escape from slavery in Egypt and features special foods and reading of the Haggadah.

rubrics_metrics.name: seizure
rubrics_metrics.description: See epilepsy.

rubrics_metrics.name: senior housing, senior apartments
rubrics_metrics.description: Age-restricted multi-unit housing with self-contained living units for older adults, usually aged 55+, who are able to care for themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senior apartments generally do not offer additional services such as meals or transportation.

rubrics_metrics.name: senior, senior citizen
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the term sparingly; can be discriminatory in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred terminology is 'older adults'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sephardi
rubrics_metrics.description: Pronounced 'suh-FAR-dee.' A Jew of Portuguese, Spanish or North African descent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originally meant descendant from the Iberian Peninsula but now often means Jews who are not Ashkenazim. Use uppercase and note plural 'Sephardim.' See Ashkenazi for comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: seroconversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientifically observable alteration of blood or other bodily fluids from HIV-negative to HIV-positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The verb is 'seroconvert.' See HIV entry for more context.

rubrics_metrics.name: seronegative
rubrics_metrics.description: Synonymous with HIV-negative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See HIV.

rubrics_metrics.name: seropositive
rubrics_metrics.description: Synonymous with HIV-positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See HIV.

rubrics_metrics.name: service animal/assistance animal/guide dog/Seeing Eye dog
rubrics_metrics.description: Service animals are trained animals, mostly dogs, which provide services to people with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal definition under ADA applies to guide dogs, signal dogs or other animals trained to do work or perform tasks for benefit of an individual with a disability. Service animal, assistance animal and guide dog are acceptable. Avoid 'Seeing Eye dog' because it is a registered trademark. Note contention around licensure/certification in disability community; best to refer to the federal definition and relevant DOJ FAQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: sex change
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid this antiquated term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See gender transition, sex reassignment for preferred terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: sexual orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes an individual's enduring physical, romantic and/or emotional attraction to another person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gender identity and sexual orientation are not the same; transgender people may be straight, lesbian, gay, or bisexual. Provide example to clarify.

rubrics_metrics.name: sexual preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Politically charged term implying sexuality is a conscious choice. Use 'sexual orientation' instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: sexual reassignment
rubrics_metrics.description: The medical and surgical process by which transgender people change their physical, sexual characteristics to reflect their gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include surgery and/or hormone therapy. It can be part of gender transition but is not necessary; not all transgender people choose or can afford surgery. Avoid overemphasizing surgery; avoid the outdated term 'sex change.'

rubrics_metrics.name: sexually transmitted infection (STI)
rubrics_metrics.description: STIs were formerly known as STDs; the new name emphasizes that anyone can be infected even without symptoms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STIs can be transmitted through vaginal, anal and oral sex, and other intimate skin-to-skin contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shabbat
rubrics_metrics.description: Hebrew word for Sabbath. The Jewish Sabbath is from sundown Friday to sundown Saturday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes common Shabbat practices: candle lighting Friday night (often by woman of house), Friday night family meal, Saturday morning services and lunch, havdalah ceremony to end Shabbat with candle and spice box; Orthodox restrictions on driving and other activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: shaman
rubrics_metrics.description: A spiritual leader in a tribal society who heals people by channeling spirits, often in an altered state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sometimes referred to as a medicine man or witch doctor. It is a description rather than a formal title; do not capitalize, even when used with a name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shariah
rubrics_metrics.description: The way or path that Muslims follow to achieve God’s will on Earth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires righteous living, protecting and expanding the community and establishing a just society; principles come from the Quran, the hadith and other considerations depending on the sect.

rubrics_metrics.name: sheesha
rubrics_metrics.description: See argilah, argeelah.

rubrics_metrics.name: sheikh
rubrics_metrics.description: Most Islamic clergymen use the title sheikh like a Christian cleric uses the Rev.; it is also used as a secular title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize when used before a name, lowercase otherwise. The term can also be used for the leader of a family, village or tribe in Arab and Arab-American communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shiism, Shiite
rubrics_metrics.description: Shiism is the name of the smaller of the two major branches of Islam; its followers are called Shiites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developed after the Prophet Muhammad's death over leadership disputes; use 'Shiite' instead of 'Shi’ah' unless in a quote or part of a name. Uppercase in all uses. See Islam, Sunni.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shinto
rubrics_metrics.description: Japan’s indigenous religion; it has no formal doctrine and stresses nature, harmony and personal cleanliness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uppercase in all references. Note historical separation from state after World War II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shiva
rubrics_metrics.description: Pronounced 'SHEE-vah.' A popular representation of God in Hinduism; worshipped as lord of time and change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also spelled Siva; note roles of Brahma and Vishnu and Shiva's consorts (Parvati, Kali, Durga).

rubrics_metrics.name: short stature
rubrics_metrics.description: See dwarf/little person/midget/short stature.

rubrics_metrics.name: sickle-cell anemia
rubrics_metrics.description: Inherited chronic anemia found chiefly among blacks, characterized by abnormal red blood cells that cause blockages and deprive organs of oxygen-carrying blood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No cure but treatable with drugs and blood transfusions; acceptable to describe a person as 'someone with sickle-cell anemia' with a short explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sikhism
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional pronunciation 'SICK-ism' but commonly 'SEEK-ism.' Originated in 15th-century Punjab; teaches equality and devotion to One Formless God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes founders, the formation of the Khalsa, Five Kakaars (articles of faith), the Guru Granth Sahib as lasting teacher, lack of clergy but use of 'guru' as spiritual guide; capitalize 'Guru' before a name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Singh
rubrics_metrics.description: A last name shared by all men who practice the Sikh religion; it means 'lion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given by Guru Gobind Singh as a sign of equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: sister, sista
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms used to refer to a family member or an affectionate, respectful name for a church member, sorority member or another black woman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of appropriateness in news copy; may use in quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: skullcap
rubrics_metrics.description: A small, close-fitting headpiece worn in some religious traditions, particularly by men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other names include yarmulke or kippa (Jews), zucchetto (Roman Catholic prelates) and kufi (Muslims).

rubrics_metrics.name: slant
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid use to describe eyes; a racial slur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See eye shape for alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: slavery
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical overview of slavery in the American colonies, growth of slave labor, Middle Passage, resistance such as the Underground Railroad, Civil War context, Emancipation Proclamation and the 13th Amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See related entries Juneteenth, Middle Passage and Underground Railroad for context; use accurate historical framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: slope
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid use to describe eyes; a racial slur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See eye shape for alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: sodomy laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Historically used to selectively persecute gay people; laws often called 'sodomy laws' were ruled unconstitutional in Lawrence v. Texas (2003).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Sodomy' should never be used to describe gay, lesbian or bisexual relationships or sexuality. See sodomy entry for more.

rubrics_metrics.name: soul food
rubrics_metrics.description: Items popular originally in the South and traditionally eaten by black people; cuisine originated during slavery supplemented by vegetables slaves grew.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Today dishes include collard greens, fried chicken, ham hocks, black-eyed peas, yams and cornbread; give historical context rather than stereotypical treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: South Asia
rubrics_metrics.description: South Asia or Southern Asia is the southern region of the Asian continent, bounded by the Indian Ocean and by West, Central, East and Southeast Asia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms 'Indian subcontinent' and 'South Asia' are both used. Lists countries included (Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal, India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka).

rubrics_metrics.name: South Asian
rubrics_metrics.description: Collective term referring to people from Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal and Sri Lanka.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also use care with 'Desi American' which is used by some but not all South Asians. Check with individuals about preferred identification and ensure race/ethnicity is essential to the content.

rubrics_metrics.name: South Asian diaspora
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains large pockets of South Asian heritage outside South Asia due to British colonial legacy and immigration; notes countries with large populations (Fiji, Guyana, Mauritius, Suriname, Trinidad and Tobago, Malaysia, Singapore, South Africa, UAE, UK, US).

rubrics_metrics.name: South Asian names (India, Pakistan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Names in South Asia and its diaspora follow dozens of complex rules and vary by community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a general rule, ask an interview subject which name is the first name and which is the surname. Be careful generalizing; many South Asian Christians, Jews, and one-word names exist. Acknowledge variation across religions, communities and generations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Southeast Asia, Southeastern Asia
rubrics_metrics.description: A subregion of Asia consisting of countries south of China, east of India, west of New Guinea and north of Australia; includes Maritime and Mainland Southeast Asia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists countries in Maritime Southeast Asia and Mainland Southeast Asia; notes heavy seismic and volcanic activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Southern Cross
rubrics_metrics.description: Confederate battle flag used during the Civil War, offensive to some black Americans because it represents the Confederacy and era of slavery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes appearance and notes appropriation by Ku Klux Klan and other racist groups; cites Southern Poverty Law Center noting use by extremist groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spanglish
rubrics_metrics.description: An informal hybrid of Spanish and English used among bilingual speakers who switch between languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linguists call it code switching; it's used when one language better expresses an idea than the other.

rubrics_metrics.name: spastic/spaz
rubrics_metrics.description: See cerebral palsy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid these derogatory terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: special rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Politically charged term used by opponents of civil rights for the LGBT community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid. Use 'LGBT rights', 'equal rights' or 'gay and lesbian rights' instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: special/special needs/functional needs
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'special needs' is now widely considered offensive because it euphemistically stigmatizes difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using these terms when describing a person with a disability or programs; exception for government references or formal organization names. Cite specific disability when possible; prefer 'functional needs' when a term is required (e.g., addressing functional needs of people with disabilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: spina bifida
rubrics_metrics.description: A neural tube defect where the spinal column does not close in the womb; most common neural tube defect in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are four types and complications range from minor to severe. Acceptable to describe someone as 'someone with spina bifida' followed by a short explanation; see Spina Bifida Association for definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: sponsorship
rubrics_metrics.description: A movement where senior professionals use clout to advocate for high-potential employees a few rungs below them, helping diversity and inclusion in leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many employers formalize sponsorship programs to achieve better DEI outcomes. Added April 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: sports stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid characterizations of black athletes as naturally better than athletes of other ethnic backgrounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such depictions are reminiscent of slavery-era stereotypes (e.g., 'bucks') and should be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sri
rubrics_metrics.description: Among some Indians it is a term of respect, similar to 'mister.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriately before a man's name where culturally relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains origin of the word and gives examples of stereotypes as 'pictures in our heads' that can be false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides examples (geisha, delivery boy, manicurist, Samurai) and cautions against stereotyping in reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stonewall
rubrics_metrics.description: The Stonewall Inn in NYC was the site of protests after a police raid in 1969 and is regarded as the birth of the modern gay civil rights movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as historical reference for LGBT rights movement context.

rubrics_metrics.name: straight
rubrics_metrics.description: Heterosexual; describes a person whose sexual and affectional attraction is to someone of the opposite sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a noun, use 'heterosexual' or 'straight person.'

rubrics_metrics.name: stricken with
rubrics_metrics.description: See victim of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid 'stricken with'—use 'victim of' guidance elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: stuttering/stammering
rubrics_metrics.description: A speech disorder characterized by repeated or prolonged words, sounds or syllables that affect fluency; often involuntary and can be accompanied by rapid blinking or lip tremors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations prefer 'stuttering' over 'stammering.' Do not refer to an individual as a 'stutterer'; use people-first language (person who stutters) and refer only if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: suffers from
rubrics_metrics.description: See victim of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid phrasing that stigmatizes; prefer neutral, people-first language when describing medical conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: suicide
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using 'commits suicide' which suggests criminal activity; instead use non-stigmatizing language like 'took his own life' or 'died by suicide.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain types of media reporting can increase suicide risk (suicide contagion). Avoid front-page dramatization or putting 'suicide' in headlines; avoid exact details of location/method; avoid dramatic photos/videos; use appropriate wording and avoid oversimplifying causes. Include context about mental health/substance abuse associations and complex factors. Consult resources: Reporting on Suicide (WHO/CDC), Dart Center tip sheets, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: suicide bombing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of explosives carried to a target on the body of the attacker or in a vehicle operated by him or her; especially fearsome because the attacker cannot be bargained with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes similarity to kamikaze and likely origin in early 1980s by Tamil Tigers.

rubrics_metrics.name: suicide contagion
rubrics_metrics.description: Research shows certain types of news coverage can increase likelihood of suicide in vulnerable individuals; magnitude relates to amount, duration and prominence of coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk increases when stories describe method, use dramatic headlines/images, or repeated sensational coverage. See suicide entry for guidance on responsible coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sunni
rubrics_metrics.description: Pronounced 'SOO-nee.' The largest denomination in Islam, followed by about 85 percent of Muslims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plural form is 'Sunnis.' See Shiism, Shiite.

rubrics_metrics.name: swastika
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the most popular symbols for Hindus, Jains and Buddhists; derived from Sanskrit meaning auspicious, luck and well-being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also note the Nazi perversion of the symbol; contextualize appropriately when reporting on symbolism.

rubrics_metrics.name: systemic racism
rubrics_metrics.description: Social values that support personal and institutional discrimination; explains how people of color must adapt to a society not built for them while white people fit in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See institutional racism for related concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tagalog
rubrics_metrics.description: Pronounced tah-GAH-log. The official language of the Philippines, but also one of many local and regional dialects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taipeng Revolution
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the bloodiest conflicts in world history; a civil war in China contemporaneous with the American Civil War, with perhaps 20 million deaths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextual note about central government's fear of separatist movements in modern Chinese history and description of leader who claimed divine status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tao
rubrics_metrics.description: Pronounced 'Dow.' The ever-changing energy of the universe in Taoism; unknowable and therefore cannot be defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Confucianism, Tao is the correct manner of conduct stemming from universal standards and ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taoism, Daoism
rubrics_metrics.description: Pronounced 'DOW-ism.' A school of philosophical and religious teachings that stem from Tao.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes suppression during Maoist rule and later revival; use appropriate capitalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tejano
rubrics_metrics.description: A Texan of Mexican descent; the term derives from 'Coahuiltejano.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes cultural elements including folk music and Tex-Mex cuisine and bilingual history.

rubrics_metrics.name: telenovela
rubrics_metrics.description: A type of limited-run television drama popular in Latin America, similar to U.S. soap operas but with distinctive qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run time is fixed, episodes shown five to six days a week, average of 120 episodes per telenovela.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thai names
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically personal name first, family name second, with long multi-syllable names, especially if Chinese.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of ordering and complexity; verify which is given name and which is surname when interviewing.
